summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and Child-Pugh class B cirrhosis, on the transplant list, was admitted with a 10-day history of malaise, weakness, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain consistent with recurrent cholangitis. She had no fevers but reported low-grade temperatures and arthralgias. Labs showed transaminitis with stable bilirubin and normal renal function. Blood and urine cultures were negative. Imaging revealed coarsened liver architecture, splenomegaly, and a gallbladder remnant with stones, but no biliary dilation or ascites. She was treated with IV antibiotics, transitioned to ertapenem, and received a PICC line for outpatient administration. Her oral vancomycin for prior C. difficile infection was continued. Her symptoms improved, liver enzymes trended downward, and MELD score improved from 10 to 8. She was discharged home with home nursing for daily IV antibiotics until transplant and instructions to continue oral vancomycin for two weeks after IV therapy completion.
